items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: Don Menza came on the lead chair and I went back to the fourth chair, which was good for me because I got a chance to kind of hang out with Art Pepper and hang out with Don, who taught me a lot. Menza taught me a lot. I mean he was like a father to me

ctx.x: I see. What were your aspirations? You went to SUNY Potsdam. I had a SUNY experience at Fredonia. And I wonder, when you went there was your jazz interest met at SUNY Potsdam?

I have to say no, but I auditioned for Fredonia first. That’s where I wanted to go because I knew that Don Menza and Sam Noto — or Don Menza had gone there. And there’s a bass player named Linc Milliman who played bass — Linc was basically from six miles outside of Mount Morris is where he grew up, so I used to play with his father, his mother and his sisters and with Linc. And I knew they went to Fredonia so I auditioned for Fredonia but they turned me down because I couldn’t sight sing. You know they made me,…

did not want me, made it difficult for me. And then there was an opening in the wind ensemble and Joe Roccisano, I don’t know if you know Joe, Joe was a great saxophone player. Joe was going to school at the time and he auditioned me on tenor to go into the wind ensemble, and he said, “Yeah, that’s good. You’ll pass. You can go in.” And my clarinet teacher balked and said, “No I don’t want him in the wind ensemble.” So with that animosity I only lasted one semester. And you know jazz was not — you know the school…
